Name: slot_vs_item_credit_permutation
Title: Slot or Item: Separating Position Credit from Content Credit in Retrieved Sets by Permutation and Leave-One-Out
Short Hypothesis: The per-position marginal value read off nested-k retrieval logs (k=1 within k=3 within k=7) confounds an item's content with its slot. Permuting the same k=3 set on the same (game, seed) separates the two. On sets whose three items share the game's task type, reversing the order is equivalent to no change within 5 net; on mixed sets, moving the single same-type item from slot 1 to slot 3 costs at least 8 net, and a planted conflicting item harms at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3. The premium is a slot-1 step, not a gradient and not lost-in-the-middle: slot 2 sits close to slot 3 on both the help side and the harm side, which is the signature of early adoption of the first item read. The nested-k rank-1 credit therefore contains a slot component of at least 8 net on mixed sets that must be removed before it is used as item credit, and the premium survives at k=7.
Related Work: Lost-in-the-middle position effects are established for long-context QA and revisited for RAG, where arxiv:2505.15561 (EMNLP 2025) finds distracting top-ranked passages matter more than position; primacy in MCQA option order (arxiv:2507.13949); demonstration-order sensitivity of in-context learning is the home literature (order permutations change few-shot accuracy; permutation-invariance violations as a source of order-induced errors, arxiv:2509.11208; PICASO arxiv:2502.17605). None permutes retrieved experience in a multi-step agent or measures the slot component of an item's leave-one-out credit. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) locates harm at the first exposed decision point but does not manipulate slot. DIG (arxiv:2509.12765) scores one document at a time and ignores order; CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) does not permute. The brief's nested-k per-position counterfactual is the object corrected here. Archived: action_prior_imprinting (5.27) and memory_budget_confound (5.63) concern priors and volume, not slot; retrieved_set_disagreement_gate (4.65) had no item-level ground truth.
Abstract: Retrieval logs that nest k=1 within k=3 within k=7 on the same games seem to give a per-position counterfactual for free, and every ranked memory system implicitly treats the rank-1 slot as the most valuable. But the item at rank 1 is both the most similar item and the first item the reader sees, so its measured credit mixes content with slot. We separate them by permutation on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader, on pools whose size is fixed before any rollout from retrieval alone and set by the minimum detectable effect rather than by what the logs happen to contain. On 200 ALL-SAME games the natural k=3 set is run in original and reversed order and tested for equivalence; on 200 MIXED games the single same-type item is shown in slot 1, 2 or 3 with the two cross-type items in fixed order, which by construction measures the slot component of that item's leave-one-out credit as an absolute net difference; on 160 procedure-type games a token-matched conflicting item is planted in slot 1, 2 or 3, giving the sign and shape of the slot effect for harm and separating a slot-1 step (early adoption) from lost-in-the-middle and recency; a k=7 arm moves the same-type item from slot 1 to slot 7. No-op repeats give the noise floor as an estimand, and every pre-registered threshold pair is separated by twice the design half-width. We predict that order is inert among consistent items, that the same-type item is worth at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3 and at least 7 net more than in slot 2, that a planted conflict harms at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3 with the drop concentrated between slots 1 and 2, and that the premium survives at k=7. The result tells the program whether its free per-position estimate is usable as item credit, by how many net points it overstates rank-1 credit on mixed sets, and how retrieval rank should be read when items are scored.
Experiments: (0) Pools, fixed before any rollout from retrieval alone (no reader calls): every natural k=3 set of the 274 validation games and of the bank-disjoint train slice is classified as ALL-SAME (three items of the game's task type), MIXED (exactly one same-type item; its natural rank 1, 2 or 3 recorded) or ALL-CROSS (dropped). Pool sizes are set from the minimum detectable effect: ALL-SAME pool = 200 games; MIXED pool = 200 games (validation first, then train slice; if natural MIXED sets run short, a MIXED set is composed from the game's own natural top-7 list as its top same-type item plus its two top cross-type items, flagged as composed and reported separately); PROC pool = 160 procedure-type games (clean, heat, cool) whose natural k=3 set is ALL-SAME, overlapping the ALL-SAME pool where possible. Reader Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas, expert bank, prompt template and item numbering held fixed, token counts logged. (1) ALL-SAME order arm (P1): O = (a,b,c) and R = (c,b,a), 200 games x 6 seeds x 2 = 2,400 episodes; no-op repeat O' on 100 games x 4 seeds = 400 episodes. (2) MIXED forced-slot arm (P2 headline, P6): the same-type item in slot 1 (S1), slot 2 (S2) or slot 3 (S3) with the two cross-type items in their natural relative order; S1 and S3 at 200 games x 8 seeds = 3,200 episodes, S2 at 200 games x 6 seeds = 1,200 episodes; no-op repeat S1' on 100 games x 4 seeds = 400 episodes. Because the residual pair is identical across S1, S2 and S3, f(S1) - f(S3) is exactly the difference between the same-type item's leave-one-out credit measured in slot 1 and in slot 3 (the LOO cell f(residual pair) cancels), i.e. the slot component of the natural-order LOO credit; no separate LOO cell is needed and none is run. (3) Planted-conflict slot arm (P3, P4): a token-matched wrong-procedure item (CONFLICT class of the pairwise audit) replaces the natural rank-3 item and is shown in slot 1 (C1), 2 (C2) or 3 (C3) with the two natural same-type items shifted in their natural order: 160 games x 8 seeds x 3 = 3,840 episodes; the unplanted reference U is the ALL-SAME O cell for PROC games inside the ALL-SAME pool and is run at 4 seeds for the rest (at most 640, expected ~250 episodes). (4) k=7 arm (P5): for the MIXED pool, the same-type item plus the six top cross-type items of the game's natural ranked list, shown with the same-type item in slot 1 (S1@7) or slot 7 (S7@7): 200 games x 4 seeds x 2 = 1,600 episodes at ~1.5x the per-episode cost of k=3. (5) Nested-k reanalysis: the logs' k=1-vs-k=0 and k=3-vs-k=1 contrasts (the free per-position profile) are re-read against the slot components measured in (2) and (4), reported as absolute net with CIs, and the corrected profile is set beside the static3 residual of Measurement C. (6) Gates, run first: C1 vs U harm >= 10 net (PROC, 4 seeds) and S1 minus the logs' k=0 >= +10 net on validation MIXED games; the no-op repeats must give |f(O') - f(O)| and |f(S1') - f(S1)| <= 5 net, otherwise the design half-widths are recomputed from the observed flip rate and the affected pool is extended by up to 100 train-slice games at 4 seeds (capped at 1,600 episodes) before any prediction is read. Total ~13,300 episodes (~14,100 k=3-equivalents), ~12 h on two A100s at the ~1,200 episodes/h of the k-sweep; arms (1)-(3) are queued as one job across both replicas so neither GPU idles.
Baselines and Ablations: No-op repeats (O', S1') as the empirical noise floor for order effects; ALL-SAME O vs R as the consistent-content control; forced-slot S1/S2/S3 on MIXED sets as the slot manipulation with the item set and the residual order fixed; planted-conflict C1/C2/C3 against the unplanted reference U to separate a slot-1 step, a gradient, lost-in-the-middle and recency on the harm side; k=7 S1@7 vs S7@7 for context length; the natural similarity order O on MIXED-LATE games (same-type item at natural rank 2 or 3, where O coincides with S2 or S3) versus S1 as the derived type-aware reordering gain; static3 from Measurement C as the type-level reference for absolute credits; composed-vs-natural MIXED sets, task type, natural rank of the same-type item and item token counts as covariates.
Falsifiable Predictions: Design half-widths (95%, cluster bootstrap over games) are calibrated from Measurement C, where 548 paired cells gave +/-5.3 net for a content contrast; order contrasts on an identical item set have at most that variance: 1,600 paired cells +/-3, 1,280 +/-3.5, 1,200 +/-3.5, 800 +/-4.5. Every threshold pair below is separated by at least twice the design half-width, so the predicted and the falsifying outcome give non-overlapping CIs; an observed value between them is reported as inconclusive, not as support. P1 (ALL-SAME, O vs R, 200 games x 6 seeds, 1,200 cells): f(R) - f(O) is equivalent to zero within +/-5 net by two one-sided tests at 5% (the 90% CI lies inside (-5, +5), which at this power requires |f(R) - f(O)| <= 2 observed). Falsified if |f(R) - f(O)| >= 8 net, the CI then lying outside the band: order matters even among consistent items. Not entailed: primacy or recency can act on consistent items, and reversal moves the most-similar item to the last slot. P2, headline (MIXED forced-slot, 200 games x 8 seeds, 1,600 cells, +/-3): f(S1) - f(S3) >= +8 net. Falsified if <= +2 net (slot-invariant reader; the CI then excludes +8). This contrast is by construction the slot component of the same-type item's LOO credit and is reported in absolute net with its CI. P3 (PROC planted, 160 games x 8 seeds, 1,280 cells, +/-3.5): harm(slot 1) - harm(slot 3) = f(C3) - f(C1) >= +8 net. Falsified if <= +1 net, including any negative value (recency dominance). P4 (same cells): the premium is a slot-1 step: D12 = f(C2) - f(C1) >= +7 net and D23 = f(C3) - f(C2) >= -1 net. Falsified if D12 <= 0 (no step between slot 1 and slot 2; a P3 premium, if present, is then a slot-3 discount rather than first-exposure adoption) or if D23 <= -8 (slot 2 is the safest slot: lost-in-the-middle). P5 (k=7, MIXED, 200 games x 4 seeds, 800 cells, +/-4.5): f(S1@7) - f(S7@7) >= +9 net. Falsified if <= 0 (the premium vanishes with longer context). P6 (MIXED S1 vs S2, 200 games x 6 seeds, 1,200 cells, +/-3.5): f(S1) - f(S2) >= +7 net (the help-side premium is also a slot-1 step). Falsified if <= 0 (slot 2 is as good as slot 1; the P2 premium is then a slot-3 penalty). Not entailed by P2, which fixes S1 - S3 and says nothing about where S2 lies between them. Derived and reported with CIs but not pre-registered: the type-aware reordering gain f(S1) - f(O) on MIXED-LATE games and the corrected nested-k per-position profile.
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts are within (game, seed) on an identical item set, so content and type credit are held fixed by construction and the static3 credit of Measurement C cancels inside every slot contrast; absolute credits (S1 - k0 and S1 - static3 on validation MIXED games, from the k-sweep and Measurement C logs) are reported against the measured +17.2 residual. Pools are fixed before rollout from retrieval alone and sized from the MDE: 1,600 cells for the headline (+/-3), 1,280 for the planted arm (+/-3.5), 1,200 for the ALL-SAME and S2 arms (+/-3.5), 800 for k=7 (+/-4.5); thresholds sit at twice the half-width. Cluster bootstrap over games (seeds nested in games) for all CIs; a permutation test over run labels within (game, seed) plus TOST for P1. The no-op repeats give the flip rate under no intervention, which is the noise-floor estimand and is checked against the Measurement-C calibration before any prediction is read (gate in Experiments 6). An ALL-SAME order null is a statement about how the reader uses consistent content (it can arise from interchangeable items as well as from an inert slot); it is the control the program needs, and the slot weight itself is identified only in the MIXED and planted cells, where content differs across slots. Reported as estimands: the flip rate, the per-game variance of the slot effect, the number of seeds at which the sign of a game's slot effect stabilizes (the per-set analogue of the per-item rank-stability count), and the reader calls per contrast at +/-3 (3,200 reader episodes per k=3 contrast). Covariates: task type (per-type reporting for every prediction), item token counts, natural rank of the same-type item (MIXED-EARLY vs MIXED-LATE), natural vs composed MIXED sets. Gates precede any null: C1 vs U >= 10 net harm and S1 - k0 >= +10 net gain.

Risk Factors and Limitations: Natural MIXED sets may be rare at the expert bank; the composed fallback keeps every item naturally retrieved for its game but forces the composition, and P2 is reported for natural and composed sets separately (the claim stands if it holds on composed sets when natural sets are too few to test, and says so). PROC games with ALL-SAME natural sets may fall short of 160 in validation; the train slice supplies the rest. The prompt's item numbering is itself an ordering cue and is held fixed. Order effects may interact with item length; token counts are a covariate. An ALL-SAME null cannot distinguish an inert slot from interchangeable items, which is why the slot weight is claimed only where content differs. Only one reader; a consumer-swap arm is outside this budget and the slot premium is claimed for Qwen3-32B. If the no-op flip rate is higher than the Measurement-C calibration implies, the capped extension in Experiments 6 is the only remedy inside the budget, and any prediction whose CI remains wider than half its threshold gap is reported as underpowered rather than as a null. Slot 2 on the help side runs at 6 seeds while slots 1 and 3 run at 8; P6 uses seeds 1-6 of S1 so its cells are paired.
Addresses gap: G12 (order and position as a component of co-retrieved-set composition in a multi-step agent) and G14 (set-level order effects on naturally retrieved sets rather than synthetic relationships: the slot manipulation is on natural items and the planted conflicting item is the only manufactured element); G15 (noise floor for order effects via no-op repeats, reported as an estimand).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: "Retrieval logs hold, per episode, the retrieved item ids in rank order, so a nested-k design already gives one crude per-position counterfactual for free"; that estimate confounds slot with content, and this idea measures the confound's size and sign in absolute net by showing the same item in different slots with the residual set fixed on the same (game, seed). Digest card arxiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap): early-decision-point adoption at the trajectory level; this idea claims a slot premium of stated size for both help and harm, its absence on consistent sets, its shape across slots 1-3 as a slot-1 step rather than a gradient or a middle dip, and its survival at k=7, none of which the card manipulates.
Changes made: P1: ALL-SAME subgroup fixed at 200 games (validation then train slice) x 6 seeds = 1,200 cells (+/-3.5); stated as a formal TOST with a +/-5 band, falsifier >= 8 net; ROT dropped from P1; the no-op repeat is the empirical null and a gate. P2: MIXED pool fixed at 200 games from the MDE rather than from the logs, 8 seeds = 1,600 cells (+/-3); falsifier moved to <= +2 so the gap is twice the half-width; the composed-set fallback is specified and reported separately. P3: PROC pool fixed at 160 games x 8 seeds = 1,280 cells (+/-3.5); falsifier <= +1 or any sign flip; the unplanted reference is needed only for the gate and is shared with the ALL-SAME O cell. P4: magnitudes pre-registered (D12 >= +7, D23 >= -1) with falsifiers D12 <= 0 or D23 <= -8, powered on the same 1,280 cells; sharpened from 'monotone' to a slot-1 step, which is the early-adoption signature and distinguishes it from a gradient as well as from lost-in-the-middle. P5: k=7 arm restricted to MIXED at 200 games x 4 seeds = 800 cells (+/-4.5) with thresholds >= +9 vs <= 0; the ALL-SAME k=7 half is cut. P6: the share-of-credit decomposition is removed because the LOO cell cancels (O minus a equals ROT minus a), so the slot component of the rank-1 LOO credit is exactly f(S1) - f(S3) and is reported in absolute net with CI as P2's estimand; the LOO-in-two-orders arm (2,192 episodes) is cut; new P6 is the help-side slot-1 step (S1 vs S2, 1,200 cells), which P2 does not entail. Budget: the 274-game O/R/ROT grid, the LOO arm, the ALL-SAME k=7 half and the ALL-CROSS cells are cut; ~13,300 episodes, ~12 h on two A100s, about 3 h more than before because every objection was power, with the arithmetic stated cell by cell. Claim kept sharp: the 8-net premium on mixed sets, the 8-net harm premium in slot 1, the ALL-SAME null and the k=7 survival are unchanged, and the mechanism is now stated more sharply as a slot-1 step on both the help and the harm side rather than a vague primacy ordering; no prediction was hedged into a measurement study.
